messages.subject: Error in buildMCMC(conf)
parts:
Hi Nimble experts,

I tried to fit the following Dirichlet process mixture model under the Chinese restaurant construction to a dataset with missing values (NAs). I added "y" to the names of variables to be monitored in order to obtain imputed values. However, an error message was reported by the buildMCMC(conf) step:

[Note] Reordering posterior_predictive samplers to execute last Error in buildMCMC(conf) : sampler_CRP: The number of nodes that are jointly clustered must be the same for each group. For example if 'mu[i,j]' are clustered such that all nodes for a given 'i' must be in the same cluster, then the number of nodes for each 'i' must be the same. Group 1 has 5 nodes being clustered where 4.7999999999999998 are expected.

I do not fully understand this error. Is there a way to fix it? Thank you very much for your help.

# Nimble model
modcode <- nimbleCode({
for(i in 1:N) {
for(j in 1:J) {
y[i, j] ~ dcat(ip[z[i], j, 1:C])
}
}
for(i in 1:N) {
for(j in 1:J) {
ip[i, j, 1:C] ~ ddirch(beta[1:C])
}
}
# CRP prior
alpha ~ dgamma(shape = 1, rate = 1)
z[1:N] ~ dCRP(conc = alpha, size = N)
})

# Run the MCMC
nMCMC <- 10000
consts <- list(N=200, J=12, C=4, beta=rep(1,4))
inits <- list(z=sample(1:5, size=consts$N, replace=TRUE))
dat <- list(y=as.matrix(data_miss))
model <- nimbleModel(modcode, data=dat, inits=inits, constants=consts)
cmodel <- compileNimble(model)
conf <- configureMCMC(model, monitors=c('ip','y'), print=TRUE)
mcmc <- buildMCMC(conf)
cmcmc <- compileNimble(mcmc, project=model)
samples <- runMCMC(cmcmc, niter=nMCMC, nburnin=0, thin=5, setSeed=TRUE)

messages.author: d78486bfff620d81
messages.subject: Re: Error in buildMCMC(conf)
parts:
Hi Cody,

This hiccup was caused by some work we did somewhat recently to reduce the amount of computation when doing MCMC with predictive nodes, in particular, by default, samplers do not condition on predictive nodes, and predictive nodes are sampled at the end of an MCMC iteration, conditional on the current parameter values in the model.

Unfortunately, this interacts in a way we didn't anticipate with how we set up the BNP/CRP sampling - for that it's necessary that sampling of each `z[i]` have the full set of dependencies, including predictive nodes. 

To get this to run, it should suffice to add this line of code at the beginning of your code:

nimbleOptions(MCMCusePredictiveDependenciesInCalculations = TRUE)

I think we'll need to add that option setting to our setup for the CRP sampling (such that you wouldn't have to do it manually), which I will think about doing for our next release, which should come in the next two weeks.

-chris
